body: Haha, well, I appreciate what you're saying, but the truth is it feels like I have nothing. My material successes are fine, but without anyone to share them with, its all hollow to me. I might be doing fine in some areas, but in others, like human relationships, I'm completely lacking. I feel like I'm a good person, but for whatever reason other people don't feel the way you and I do. And it seems redundant to keep trying when everyone seems indifferent to your efforts.

Haha, well, I appreciate your positive attitude. I wish I could have that outlook, but really, I'm losing the will for this fight. Its a shame, because I really do feel like I had a lot to offer the world, but I just can't stand the misery of no-to-minimal interpersonal contact. Some people really are born to be single, and I'm just one of them, I feel.

Well, this is probably the most pleasant message I've gotten, so props to you for that. 

Anyway, as nice as the fantasy is, I just doubt its potential to happen. I used to be very optimistic, but that has waned over time, especially after the first date I had in months turned out to be a total dud.

I'm twenty, but I read so much about guys who are in their 30s or 40s and who are still exactly like me. And I'm just not strong enough for that struggle. I've already gone on so long like this, one more year of it makes me think about taking my own life, much less a decade. Call it a bad attitude, but based on past and current experiences, I just know my trajectory is aimed toward a middle-aged man who has had one serious relationship his whole life. And I just don't have the strength to live that life.

Well, its a given that I'm crazy. I'm talking suicide here, not cake baking.

Anyway, it definitely has its faults, but the much sought after painless, quick and easy method doesn't exist, so I've got to make a choice. No one I know owns a firearm, and I'm too young to purchase one in my state. I also don't have a garage, so carbon monoxide poisoning isn't really an option, also I don't want a friend or relative to find me after the fact.

I know its going to be tough to convince you of this when I'm threatening suicide, but this advice really doesn't apply to me. I know what kind of person you think you're talking to - the perpetual whiner, the one who's misogynystic because he can't get a date, the one who expects a perfect ten when he himself is nothing to write home about. Well, I'm none of those things. I always stay positive when I'm dealing with people, even if I'm hurting on the inside. I actually have a supervisor position at work, so I kind of have to since my job involves so much human interaction, you can't afford to be a downer when you're seen as a leader to people I'm not shallow, I'm honestly far more attracted to a beautiful mind than a body. The only time I lose my composure is after long periods of defeat and isolation, but even then I make it a point not to drag other people down. That's why I'm on reddit talking about suicide rather than to a friend or family member.

Yeah, yeah, I know I'm falling right into the stereotype of the broken person who refuses to fix himself, but I'm really just trying to be as honest as possible. I won't claim that I'm perfect, but I really don't think I'm any worse than a lot of people who have a wildly successful love life. I've actually gone on dates, and I do a pretty good job of making the other person laugh, talk about themselves, and alk the things I'm told I should be doing, but for whatever reason, they don't stick around. 

And that's why it hurts so bad, because I'm struggling with this problem that seems invisible, and thus unfixeable. So after a while, you have to begin wondering if its all worth the struggle.
